FR-11 The system shall display contact names or fallback identifiers (phone/email) in the list.

FR-12 The system shall allow the user to view detailed information of a selected contact.

FR-14 The system shall allow editing any field of an existing contact.

FR-15 The system shall update the stored contact data immediately after saving edits.

FR-30 The system shall allow unmarking a contact as favorite.

FR-42 The system shall allow sending SMS from a contact.

FR-44 The system shall allow sending email from a contact.

FR-47 The system shall allow importing contacts from external storage files.

FR-61 The system shall allow restoring contacts from backup.

Document: Samsung Contacts Application

Functional requirements summary:
- FR-1: Create contact with at least one phone/email.
- FR-2, FR-3: Support multiple phone numbers/emails per contact.
- FR-4: Optional fields (address, org, notes, photo).
- FR-5: Validate presence of phone/email before saving.
- FR-6, FR-7: Validate phone/email formats.
- FR-8: Save to local/SIM/cloud storage.
- FR-9, FR-10, FR-11: Display scrollable contact list with names/fallback IDs.
- FR-12, FR-13: View/edit all contact fields in detail view.
- FR-14, FR-15: Edit and save contact updates immediately.
- FR-16, FR-17, FR-18: Delete single/multiple contacts with confirmation.
- FR-19: Remove deleted contacts from groups.
- FR-20-FR-25: Search by name/phone/email (partial, case-insensitive, dynamic).
- FR-26-FR-28: Sort alphabetically by first/last name (handle nameless contacts).
- FR-29-FR-32: Mark/unmark favorites with persistent status.
- FR-33-FR-39: Manage groups (create, rename, delete, add/remove contacts).
- FR-40-FR-45: Initiate calls/SMS/emails via external apps.
- FR-46-FR-49: Import from SIM/VCF (handle duplicates).
- FR-50-FR-52: Export selected/all contacts to VCF.
- FR-53-FR-58: Sync with cloud (auto/manual, conflict resolution).
- FR-59-FR-63: Backup/restore with notifications.
- FR-64-FR-67: Detect/suggest/merge duplicates.
- FR-68-FR-70: Manage profile photos (add/remove/display).
- FR-71: Fast scrolling for large lists.
- FR-72, FR-73: Multi-select mode with cancel option.
- FR-74: Ensure UI-storage consistency.
- FR-75: Handle large contact data.
- FR-76: View contact source (SIM/local/cloud).
- FR-77: Restrict editing read-only contacts.
- FR-78, FR-79: Copy/share contact details (VCF for sharing).
- FR-80: Generate VCF for sharing.
- FR-81-FR-83: Handle permissions (restrict/resume functionality).
- FR-84: Display error messages for invalid operations.
- FR-85: Block saving invalid contacts.
- FR-86: Undo recent deletes (if supported).
- FR-87, FR-88: Track/modify timestamps.
- FR-89, FR-90: Ensure unique contact IDs.
- FR-91, FR-92: Support custom fields.
- FR-93, FR-94: Link/maintain related contacts.
- FR-95, FR-96: Support/normalize international phone numbers.
- FR-97, FR-98: Handle special characters/multilingual names.
- FR-99, FR-100: Maintain performance under high data volume and UI-data sync.

Non-functional requirements summary:
- Not explicitly listed in the provided SRS.

Validation and constraints:
- Validate phone/email formats (FR-6, FR-7).
- Ensure at least one phone/email per contact (FR-5).
- Unique group names per account (FR-34).
- Handle duplicates during import/merge (FR-49, FR-64-FR-67).
- Permission handling (FR-81-FR-83).
- Conflict resolution during sync (FR-58).
- Data consistency (FR-74, FR-100).

Coverage priorities for next tests:
- Core CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete).
- Validation (phone/email formats, required fields).
- Search and sorting functionality.
- Group management and favorite marking.
- Import/export (VCF handling, duplicates).
- Sync and backup/restore flows.
- Permission handling and error states.
- Performance under large datasets (FR-75, FR-99).
- UI consistency and real-time updates (FR-100).

post.description:
View it in Neo4j Browser

Open:

http://localhost:7474

Login with:

username: neo4j
password: jms12345

Then run this Cypher query:

MATCH (p:Project {name: "contacts-app"})-[:HAS_SRS]->(s:SRS)-[:HAS_CHUNK]->(c:Chunk)
RETURN p, s, c
ORDER BY c.order;

This will show the project, SRS node, and all 17 chunk nodes.

View only chunk text
MATCH (:Project {name: "contacts-app"})-[:HAS_SRS]->(:SRS)-[:HAS_CHUNK]->(c:Chunk)
RETURN c.order AS order, c.text AS chunk_text
ORDER BY order;
View SRS summary
MATCH (:Project {name: "contacts-app"})-[:HAS_SUMMARY]->(sum:Summary {kind: "srs"})
RETURN sum.text AS srs_summary;
View full SRS text
MATCH (:Project {name: "contacts-app"})-[:HAS_SRS]->(s:SRS)
RETURN s.id, s.source_path, s.text;
View graph-style overview
MATCH (p:Project {name: "contacts-app"})
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:HAS_SUMMARY|HAS_SRS|HAS_FIGMA|HAS_TEST|HAS_FEATURE]->(n)
OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[r]->(m)
RETURN p, n, r, m
LIMIT 500;

Your local_rag_api.py also has a /graph/cypher endpoint that returns ready-to-run Neo4j Explore queries for this kind of graph inspection.
